name: Hotel Ritz Paris
positioning: Historic palace hotel on Place Vendôme in central Paris, opened in 1898 by César Ritz and Auguste Escoffier
best_for: History buffs drawn to the hotel's Chanel and Hemingway connections
Food lovers who want to take a cooking class at the hotel's own school
Travelers who want a classic, gilded Paris hotel with a pool and spa

facts.text: The hotel is at 15 Place Vendôme, 75001 Paris.
In 2012 the hotel closed for the first time in its history and reopened four years later with updated technologies and new facilities.
A grand staircase winds up from the lobby.
Higher-floor rooms and most suites have balconies or terraces.
Rooms have signature details such as key-shaped light switches and silk tulip lampshades.
Bar Vendôme is a glass-ceilinged brasserie that serves a Japanese breakfast in the morning.
Afternoon tea with madeleines is served in the Salon Proust.
The Ritz Bar, launched in September 2021, is a lantern-topped space serving cocktails inspired by astrological signs.
The hotel has a pool and a central garden.
Treatments include La Prairie facials and massages with French-made oils formulated specially for Ritz Paris.
There is a David Mallett hair salon, a nail bar and a makeup area, plus a shopping arcade with luxury boutiques and a Ritz concept store.

highlights.text: Swiss hotelier César Ritz partnered with French chef Auguste Escoffier to open the hotel in 1898.
Coco Chanel lived at the hotel for 34 years and has a suite named for her; Ernest Hemingway, another regular, gives his name to both a suite and a bar.
Guests can book a class at the Ecole Ritz Escoffier cooking school, which also offers classes for kids.
The marble bathrooms keep peach-colored robes and towels, a hue chosen by Mr. Ritz, and golden swan bathtub taps.
All rooms have marble fireplaces, and the design of each Prestige Suite aims to reflect its namesake, with antique books lining the Marcel Proust suite.

considerations.text: Most rooms have no coffee or tea making facilities, so coffee and tea are ordered from room service.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's palace status.
WhataHotel notes the formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers.
